newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks set for calmer trading this week.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks set for calmer trading this week.

text.p: Hong Kong's stock market is expected to refocus on fundamentals this the week and could trade sideways for much of the time, although hopes of healthy corporate earnings may provide a positive bias, analysts said.
The market had a rocky ride last week, quaking on concerns about the health of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping then rallying after his death cleared the uncertainty.

"The political stuff is out of the way so we have to look at other things," said Geoff Galbraith, institutional sales trader at NAVA SC Securities. "I think now we are going to get back to interest rates and asset allocations."
The Hang Seng Index rose 331.59 points, or 2.53 percent, last week to close at 13,444.85 on Friday. The gains included a 305-point surge on Thursday following Deng's death.

"On the fundamental side there is not much change," said Kelvin Tang, an analyst at ImPac Asset Management. "Investors are still keeping to the sidelines to see if there is a more obvious trend for the market to go up."

HSBC Holdings Plc is due to release its 1996 results on March 3 and some analysts said investors may position themselves ahead of the results and push prices higher, particularly in the banking sector.
"People will want to get into banks ahead of that," said Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager at Nikko Securities.
But he said there were no other reasons why the market should really push ahead. He saw mostly sideways trading.

"People will buy the market ahead (of the results) and the outcome will drive the subsequent performance," said DBS Securities director of research Percy Au-Young. He put the trading range in the week ahead at 13,100 to 13,600 points.
Hong Kong and China Gas Co Ltd is due to release its 1996 results on Thursday.

Ben Kwong, director of research at Dharmala Securities, said as well as looking at forthcoming earnings results, investors were also anticipating strong demand for new residential property sales which could hit the market soon.
He said the Hang Seng Index could try to test 13,800 points.
"I think the market will move up next week. Everyone expects a better performance in March because there will be more news like corporate results," said Kwong.
"There will be major residential units on sale in March and I also expect the reponse to be quite good. All this will be taken as an excuse to buy again."

One residential property sale which the market is eagerly awaiting is Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd's joint residential development project with China Light & Power Co Ltd in Hung Hom on the Kowloon peninsula.
But Ricky Tam, senior research analyst at Delta Asia Securities, said as investors turn to fundamentals again, interest rate concerns could resurface.
Data released in the United States in March could show strong economic growth, he said.
"I think the downtrend will resume next week. The market will test 13,000," said Tam.
